newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran disabled war veterans march on German embassy.
newsitem.headline: Iran disabled war veterans march on German embassy.

text.p: Some 3,000 Iranian veterans disabled in Iraqi chemical attacks marched on Germany's embassy in Tehran on Wednesday to protest at a Berlin court verdict accusing Iran of ordering political killings, witnesses said.

Rows of demonstrators -- many of them in wheelchairs, some wearing gasmasks -- carried pictures of troops killed in chemical attacks during the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq war. They were backing demands to bring to justice German firms which allegedly supplied toxic chemicals to Baghdad, the witnesses said.

The demonstrators, some of whom carried effigies of the German court judge, demanded an apology from Bonn for the charges that Iranian leaders ordered the 1992 killings of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.
Iran has repeatedly denied any role in the slayings, which it blames on infighting between opposition groups.

The demonstrators, some of whom had come from other parts of Iran, gathered earlier in front of a clinic treating victims of chemical attacks. From there they marched across central Tehran to the embassy which was surrounded by rows of police in riot gear.
Marchers carried a mock chemical weapon missile which bore the flags of Israel and the United States, in reference to Iranian charges that the German verdict was provoked by Iran's two arch-enemies.
Some protesters they would hold a sit-in in front of the embassy after the demonstration, which was orderly.

It was the fourth demonstration at the barricaded embassy after the Thursday verdict sparked a diplomatic row between Iran and Germany, until recently Tehran's main trade partner and most important Western friend.
Tehran has said court proceedings would begin shortly against 24 German companies accused of having helped Iraq produce chemical weapons during the war.
Iran has responded to the recalling for consultations of all European Union ambassadors, except Greece's, by announcing it would reciprocate.
